note: This stage executes reviewed connective focus forms only after an overt preceding clause boundary. A standalone connective form is left unjudged rather than assumed to have omitted context.

rule: For reviewed common-noun true subject focus in the second clause, ayaana/baana inherits the same absolute/non-subject case requirement as base ayaa/baa.
After removing only connective -na, predicate agreement is delegated unchanged to the reviewed restrictive subject-focus analyzer for base ayaa/baa.

ayaana/baana are not negative-focus markers, and buuna/beyna are not true focused-subject markers. ayaan remains the distinct negative-focus spelling already modeled elsewhere. No unattested clitic+na paradigm is generated from the reviewed forms.
In overt second-clause focus, connective -na may attach after a reviewed baa+subject-clitic form. Remove only -na internally and preserve the encoded subject person(s).
For reviewed buuna/beyna second-clause focus, the subject clitic must be compatible with an exact independently reviewed finite verb form. The focused phrase does not control this agreement.

Standalone buuna/beyna, unknown following verbs, and predicted forms such as baadna/baanna/baydinna remain unjudged until independently evidenced and modeled. The checker does not infer the antecedent of uu/ay and does not infer whether the focused phrase is object, adverbial, or another non-subject constituent.
